text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said that Pakistan no longer exists ideologically and warned that it was in danger of suffering fragmentation in the next 20 years.
- Deposed prime minister Benazir Bhutto alleged that President Farooq Leghari was trying to force her party to boycott elections and vowed not to oblige him.
- Pakistan Muslim Leaque chief Nawaz Sharif kicked off his party's election campaign with a rally in Karachi.
- President Farooq Leghari reiterated the government's determination to hold free and fair elections on February 3.
- Rana Muhammad Nazir, a former member of the National Assembly (lower house) belonging to the Pakistan Muslim League, was arrested by the Federal Investigation Agency in Lahore.
- British Prime Minister John Major starts a visit this week to India, Pakistan and Bangladesh aimed at promoting trade.
- The Commerce Ministry has prepared three relief packages to increase exports.

- The tight credit policy pursued by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan has adversely affected raw cotton buying from ginning factories, which have accumulated unsold stocks of over 1.8 million 375-lb bales.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Almost all corporations and departments working under the Petroleum and Natural Resources Ministry are being investigated for possible corruption and irregularities, the secretary at the ministry said.
- A joint venture with Korea's Daewoo is being set up to manufacture motorcycles, sources said.
- The 28.7 billion rupees rehabilitation and expansion project of state-run Sui Southern Gas Co, scheduled to have been completed in 1996, has shown poor progress, sources said.
FINANCIAL POST

- The garment manufacturing industry is facing its worst crisis as 1,400 to 2,200 factories have closed and only 800 are operating, the president of the Pakistan Ready-made Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association, Pervaiz Hanif, said.
THE NATION

- President Farooq Leghari said the caretaker government was considering setting up a National Security Council comprising the president, prime minister, joint services chief, heads of army, navy and air force, as well as the defence, finance and interior ministers to deliberate on economic and security issues. But Prime Minister Meraj Khalid said he has no information about its establishment.
- Customs authorities seized 12 million rupees from a Dubai-bound flight before its departure.
- The Milli Yekjehti Council, an alliance of five religious parties, decided to contest the elections in spite of the boycott announced by one of its members, Jamaat-i-Islami.
THE NEWS
- Importers accused the pre-shipment inspection companies of collecting an extra 250 million rupees in violation of rules.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
